content: Studies that fail to define children at risk, or do not provide sufficient clarity, as well as those that only report the number of infections without further analysis, are not scored on this criterion. 1. Rate of Transmission: a) The rate of transmission should include a denominator that specifies the number of children at risk. b) The number of HIV transmissions should also be reported. 2. Outcome Stratified by Feeding Type: a) If outcomes are stratified by feeding type, this is noted as Yes. b) If outcomes are not stratified by feeding type, this is noted as No. 3. Adequacy of Follow-Up in Cohort Studies: a) Complete follow-up is achieved when all subjects are accounted for. b) If subjects lost to follow-up are unlikely to introduce bias and the number lost is small (less than 20%), this is acceptable. c) If the follow-up rate is less than 20% and there is no description of those lost to follow-up, this is a limitation. d) If no statement regarding follow-up is provided, this is also noted. This information is detailed in Appendix 5.
